incident_summary: EDGC event 116181 reports forced-normal standby-power status while a fault persists. Preserved SIEM and user-supplied master-timeline posts establish a reported sequence from SMR enumeration and DCS divergence through display discrepancies, retained-credential access, RMS record alteration, EDGC masking and supervisor discovery. Contributors confirm some feed rows but challenge event origin, propagation and physical consequences. One campaign/actor is stipulated, not independently attributed. Security reporting is warranted on the simulated facts; safety/material reportability remains conditional on functional and material evidence.
assessment_status: Evidence-qualified analysis finalized with available evidence on 2026-10-29 UTC. Six user-supplied owner posts and the master log are incorporated; RMS's unavailable analysis remains an explicit dependency. Live NRC regulatory text was retrieved through the MCP Fetch reference server from Cornell after official-site MCP access failed; government eCFR was cross-checked separately. Unresolved functional/material facts are not presented as verified. No actual regulator notifications made.

clock.how_start_was_reconstructed: Jeremiah's DCS system post and later master-log confirmation align with preserved 116173: first reported source divergence on October 9 08:47Z, exactly 14 days before supervisor discovery. October 14 DCS 116174 at 06:33 precedes RPS 116176 at 07:06 and SFPCM 116177 at 07:40, but chronology does not establish propagation. Jeremiah disputes what 1012 denotes; Sindi cannot validate the level discrepancy. Thus the reconstructed start is earliest reported adverse-integrity evidence, not proof of origin, first foothold or qualifying legal discovery. EDGC alone exposes only October 22 masking.
clock.clock_rule: Keep occurrence, telemetry receipt, operator recognition, qualifying-trigger discovery, emergency declaration, and student collection distinct. 73.77 and 74.11 explicitly run from discovery, whereas 50.72(b) uses occurrence language and 50.72(b)(3)(v) describes a condition at discovery. Scenario wording about the earliest observable act does not override each regulation's trigger. Earlier recorded evidence warrants investigation of earlier discovery; it does not prove a human recognized a reportable cyberattack then.

safety.authority: NRC-NRR / 10 CFR 50; initial recipient is Operations Center, not a separate office mailbox
safety.notification_deadline: If 50.72(b)(3)(v) is met, as soon as practical and within 8 hours under (b)(3); determine when the qualifying condition was discovered. Seriously degraded or unanalyzed conditions under (b)(3)(ii) also carry 8 hours from occurrence. Emergency-class declaration invokes (a)(3): immediately after appropriate State/local notification, no later than 1 hour after declaration. Listed (b)(2) events have 4 hours from occurrence; a cyber incident alone does not establish one.
safety.notification_recipient: NRC Operations Center via ENS; fallback telephone or other effective method under 50.72(a)(2). Appropriate State/local agencies under the approved emergency plan if an emergency is declared.
safety.regulatory_basis: 10 CFR 50.72(a)(1)-(3), (b)(2), (b)(3)(ii), (b)(3)(v)-(vi), (c); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-10/section-50.72 (retrieved live 2026-10-26). Evaluate independent LER criteria in 50.73(a)(2), including (v); qualifying LER due within 60 days after discovery under 50.73(a)(1): https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-10/chapter-I/part-50/section-50.73.
safety.classification_basis: Tiffany's RPS journal/watcher observations support no documented later protection-logic/bypass change or actual trip: power logs range 995-1005, no coil writes after October 13 15:46:46Z, and scripted pressure excursions do not trip. These shared-account records are tamperable and do not cover the complete October 9 onward window. She infers a corrupted DCS-carried display but cannot identify it and confirms no built diode/link; Jeremiah and Dylan dispute the 1012 meaning/path and report different downstream values. Sindi's discrepancy has no local/source counterpart and unconfirmed safety effect; earlier alarms fit restarts. EDGC masking does not establish loss of the entire required power function. No valid actuation, required shutdown, qualifying unanalyzed condition or prevented safety function is established under 50.72; available redundancy and engineering assessment remain unknown. A 73.77 safety-related digital impact does not itself establish a separate 50.72 notification.

open_questions: When was a condition capable of preventing the whole required safety function first discovered, and which other trains remained operable?

Did any event require a Technical Specification shutdown, valid reportable actuation, emergency classification, or establish an unanalyzed condition? Obtain shift logs and engineering determination, not just displayed values.

What implemented point does SIEM egen_status name, and what underlying fault persisted? Current engine-running with fuel zero is explained by simulator source and cannot answer that historical question.

safety.resolution_test: Verified independent indications, restored credited equipment/functions, documented operability and Technical Specification actions, and validated surveillance; a normal status bit alone is not restoration.

security.notification_deadline: Treat confirmed campaign impairment of credited monitoring/status functions as the 73.77(a)(1) 1-hour-after-discovery branch, pending prompt functional confirmation. At minimum the covered potential-impact branch (a)(2)(i) is 4 hours after discovery. Do not wait for attribution. The 8-hour (a)(3) reconnaissance-information clock is separate and not a substitute once impact exists. Corrective-action records within 24 hours of discovery under (b); qualifying written security followup within 60 days of telephone notification under (d).
security.notification_recipient: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS; fallback methods under 73.77(c)(1). Written report under 73.4 with copy to Director, NSIR or designee per 73.77(d)(4).
security.regulatory_basis: 10 CFR 73.77(a)(1), (a)(2)(i)-(ii), (a)(3), (b), (c)(1), (c)(7), (d); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-10/section-73.77 (retrieved live 2026-10-26). 73.54 defines protected functional scope; it is not the notification timing provision.
security.clock_start_source: Jeremiah's DCS system post supports October 9 08:47Z as the earliest reported adverse divergence, possibly later than invisible initial access. Sarah instead proposes the 07:24 SMR enumeration as initial access; this remains unverified. Dylan and Tiffany adopt DCS's bound, while their local candidates are October 14 06:49 and 07:06. PSI entry is October 17 05:16Z, later still. Discovery of discrepant coolant readings is October 23 08:47Z. None supplies exact recognition of a qualifying cyberattack/functional impact. Do not adopt a blanket claim that choosing SMR versus DCS can never affect reporting: reconnaissance receipt under 73.77(a)(3) and adverse/potential cyber discovery under (a)(1)/(2) have distinct triggers, even if a headline start alone does not set those legal clocks.

Did stale-credential use reflect personnel access under 73.77(a)(2)(ii), a stolen credential, or another path?

Sindi's runbook records removal of the EDGC partner key on October 21, but explicitly does not re-verify the workstation key's authorization on PSI after the October 22 agent-forwarded test. Can PSI's owner confirm the historical key lifecycle and distinguish the authorized test from the incident?

safeguards.authority: NRC-NMSS / 10 CFR 74; Part 75 for applicable US-IAEA safeguards obligations
safeguards.notification_deadline: 74.11(a): within 1 hour of discovery of loss, theft, unlawful diversion or attempted theft/diversion of SNM for covered possessors (at least 1 gram contained U-235, U-233 or plutonium possessed). The gram threshold is not a minimum loss threshold. Measured discards and inventory differences are excepted from that one-hour requirement. 75.36(b): immediately make a special report by telephone to NRC for applicable loss, unexpected containment change permitting unauthorized removal, or license-condition triggers; not a generic 24-hour IAEA report.
safeguards.notification_recipient: NRC Operations Center under 74.11(b), via ENS if a party, otherwise effective fallback; special report to NRC by telephone under 75.36(b). NRC furnishes covered Part 75 information to IAEA under 75.13(a); a direct licensee-to-IAEA call is not established here.
safeguards.classification_basis: RMS 116180 at October 20 02:59Z reports record alteration, not proven loss or attempted diversion. Dylan relays the same row. Jeremiah reports no DCS 40006 write near that time and notes repeated values associated with other command writes; this limits observable downstream propagation, not the possibility of RMS record alteration or material loss. No material inventory, containment-change finding, Part 75 designation or applicable loss/license condition is supplied. The scenario stipulates all three frameworks, but specific 74.11/75.36 legal triggers still require those missing facts.
coordination_gaps: User reports Tamas's RMS analysis is not ready. Use preserved 116180 and named cross-system sources now; independent instrument/transaction/physical-inventory reconciliation remains unconfirmed, not grounds to delay an otherwise required notification.

Dylan's PSI entry/read records show no material movement or seal/containment change, and Dominick's later tamper alarms establish neither physical entry nor an incident connection. Those missing material facts and facility Part 75 conditions remain unresolved.
open_questions: Did falsification conceal loss or attempted diversion, or only corrupt a record? What quantity/isotope and independent physical evidence support the answer?
When did the licensee discover any qualifying loss, attempt or containment change, independently of record alteration time?
Is the facility selected/notified under 75.7(a), subject to another relevant agreement, and what loss limits or special-report license conditions apply?
safeguards.resolution_test: Independent physical/material reconciliation and restored continuity of knowledge, including seals/surveillance where applicable, with regulator-agreed corrections. Rebuilding a database or revoking a credential does not establish that material stayed in place.
